scripts.dartProcessClean.label: Clean leaked Dart processes
scripts.dartProcessClean.description:
Kill the leaked Dart/Flutter tool-host processes that accumulate on Windows and starve VS Code of CPU and RAM.

Repeated flutter invocations (test, pub get, gen-l10n) spawn dart.exe and dartvm.exe hosts that are orphaned when the parent is killed or crashes. They are detached from VS Code, so restarting the editor does not reclaim them — they accumulate (observed: 142 processes, ~2.8 GB) until the extension host hangs.

Kills: every dartvm.exe (flutter CLI VM host), dart.exe flutter_tools hosts, and orphaned flutter_tester.exe.
Keeps: language-server, tooling-daemon, devtools, development-service (DDS), flutter_agent_lens — the live services VS Code needs.

Windows only. Runs with --yes (no confirmation prompt). Pass --dry-run via Set Params to preview without killing. Pass --include-dds when no app is being debugged, or --include-build-runner when no watch is running.
scripts.runTest.label: Run Flutter tests (safe)
scripts.runTest.description:
Run Flutter tests with automatic orphan cleanup on Windows.

flutter test on Windows copies native assets (e.g. sqlite3.dll) into build/native_assets/windows/ on every run. When a previous flutter_tester.exe is still alive it keeps that DLL memory-mapped, so the next run crashes with PathAccessException: Deletion failed (OS Error: Access is denied, errno = 5).

This script kills any lingering flutter_tester.exe processes first, then runs flutter test --no-pub against the given test paths. flutter_tester.exe is the headless test engine — never the user's app (device/desktop apps run as <appname>.exe).

Defaults to running all tests in the test/ directory when no paths are specified. Set specific test file paths via Set Params (e.g. test/foo_test.dart).
scripts.dailyReport.label: Daily Git change report
scripts.dailyReport.description:
Generate a detailed JSON report of recent Git changes to Dart, JSON, YAML, asset, and localization files.

Analyzes Git history for the last day and produces a structured report including: a summary of all commits, per-file status (added, modified, deleted), textual diffs, file type classification (Dart widgets, JSON keys, pubspec dependency changes, asset status, ARB localization keys), the latest commit details per file, heuristic code-analysis hints (error handling, public API, UI keywords, performance keywords), and related test files modified in the same commits.

The report is written to a timestamped file and opened automatically. Requires Git on PATH and the PyYAML Python package (pip install PyYAML).
scripts.flutterSdkRepair.label: Repair Flutter SDK
scripts.flutterSdkRepair.description:
Comprehensive repair of the Flutter SDK and Dart analyzer plugin system.

Fixes: "Unable to find AOT snapshot for dartdev", "Could not find directory at .../devtools", "'dart compile' does not support build hooks", "No response for request CustomLintRequest.analyzerPluginRequest", and custom_lint/saropa_lints not loading.

Steps: (1) terminates all Dart, Java, and Gradle processes that may hold file locks, (2) deletes the Flutter SDK cache (bin/cache) to force a complete rebuild, (3) clears the Dart analyzer plugin manager cache (.dartServer/.plugin_manager), (4) clears local VS Code extension caches, (5) cleans the global pub cache, (6) rebuilds the SDK via flutter doctor, (7) restores project dependencies with flutter pub get, (8) optionally tests custom_lint.

Close VS Code and all IDEs first. Run from an elevated terminal for best results.
scripts.dependencyReport.label: Flutter dependency report
scripts.dependencyReport.description:
Generate a dependency health report for a Flutter project.

Default mode is read-only: shows project info (Flutter/Dart versions, platform targets), the full dependency tree, outdated packages with current vs. latest versions, and any dependency overrides. Results are written to a timestamped log file.

Optional flags via Set Params: --interactive (prompt y/n before each upgrade step for Kotlin, Firebase, packages), --upgrade (auto-upgrade all packages), --verbose (show blocked packages and debug output).

Requires Flutter on PATH and the PyYAML Python package (pip install PyYAML). The tqdm progress bar package is used if available but not required.

releaseBoard.keywords.label.title: Keywords and phrases
releaseBoard.keywords.label.intro: These words decide how serious a document looks to the board. A document gets the highest level whose phrases score at least the threshold. Change them where the board guesses wrong. Nothing is saved until you press Save and confirm.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.warn: Careful: taking a phrase out of a higher level, or putting one into Low, can lower the severity of documents. A lower severity can turn a red light green, because the document then no longer stops the release. Read the preview before you save.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewTitle: How many open documents on the board would get a different severity with your edits. It updates as you type. Nothing is changed until you save.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewInval: A value is not valid, so there is no preview.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewNone: No open document on the board would change level.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewSumma: {changed} of {checked} open documents would change level: {lowered} lower, {raised} higher.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewEase: {count} would stop the release no longer. The light could turn greener.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewTight: {count} would start to stop the release.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewUnche: None of the {total} open documents could be checked, so the effect on them is unknown.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewParti: Only {checked} of {total} open documents were checked, so the effect on the others is unknown.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.previewListT: Examples of documents that would change level. Documents that would stop the release no longer come first.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.help_extreme: Money and the store: payments, purchases, billing, refunds, prices. A document that scores here is Extreme.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.help_critica: Losing data, security and privacy, crashes, and anything that blocks a release. A document that scores here is Critical.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.help_high: How people start and keep using the app: first run, sign-in, install, permissions, ratings. A document that scores here is High.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.help_low: Small things: typos, polish, wording, refactors. A document is Low when only these score and nothing higher does.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.mediumNote: Medium has no phrases. A document is Medium when no level reaches the threshold.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.levelTip: {level} phrases. {count} in the list. Click to fold or unfold.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.phrasesHint: A phrase is plain text. Letters do not matter. It must start at the beginning of a word and may end inside one, so overwrit also finds overwrite. There are no patterns and no wildcards.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.inputTip: Type a phrase for the {level} list, then press Enter or the Add button.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.addTip: Add the typed phrase to the {level} list.

releaseBoard.keywords.label.changedTip: This list differs from the shipped one.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.scoringTip: How many points a level needs, and how much a phrase is worth where it is found. Click to fold or unfold.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.thresholdHel: Points a level needs before a document gets it. Lower means more documents reach the higher levels.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.wTitleHelp: Points for a phrase in the file name or the first heading.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.wHeadHelp: Points for a phrase in the first 20 lines.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.wBodyHelp: Points for a phrase later in the document. Counted only when phrases are frequent enough.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.wCapHelp: Most times one phrase counts in one part of a document, so a repeated word cannot decide alone.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.negTip: Words that cancel a phrase. Click to fold or unfold.
releaseBoard.keywords.label.negHelp: A phrase right after one of these words does not count. For example no refund does not count as refund.
